memories.content: Define in one sentence the user groups and usage contexts to which the design knowledge does not apply.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through explicitly excluded targets and situations.
Specify user goals, interaction conditions, and technological constraints under which the proposed design knowledge can be transferred.
Small-scale formative studies can support analytic generalization distinct from statistical representativeness when results are expressed in terms of design conditions and mechanisms.
The author of this proposal tends to apply design knowledge derived from an accessible sample to a broader user population.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames address independent concerns: the reference defines boundaries for transferring and generalizing design knowledge, while the compared frame governs participant compensation, payment methods, burden accounting, and staff labor distinctions. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: Both memories express the one-sided claim that explicit exclusions define and communicate where results do not apply.
relations.summary: Design knowledge should state excluded user groups and contexts so its generalization boundary can be judged.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no claim about conditions for transferring design knowledge.
relations.summary: Transferability should be specified through user goals, interaction conditions, and technological constraints.

relations.reason: The compared frame contains no claim about evidentiary forms of generalization.
relations.summary: Small formative studies can support analytic rather than statistically representative generalization when framed through design conditions and mechanisms.

relations.reason: This one-sided diagnostic observation has no compensation-related counterpart.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to extend design knowledge from an accessible sample to a broader population.

relations.reason: Both memories express the underlying one-sided claim that total participation burden should govern compensation.
relations.summary: Compensation budgets and perceived fairness should reflect session time plus required technical and travel preparation.

relations.reason: Both memories split the one-sided policy of paying for actual session participation.
relations.summary: Participants should be compensated for time actually spent in sessions, including when they withdraw midway and regardless of modality.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no claim about alternative payment instruments.
relations.summary: Remote participants unable to use electronic transfers may receive equal-value gift cards.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no claim about when compensation logistics must be resolved.
relations.summary: An unresolved payment method should not be treated as a proposal-stage deficiency.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no claim about burden-based compensation differences between modalities.
relations.summary: On-site and remote compensation may differ when their travel or technical-preparation burdens differ.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no claim about compensating longitudinal reporting effort.
relations.summary: Longitudinal compensation calculations should include time spent recording diary entries and repeated reports outside sessions.

relations.reason: The reference frame contains no claim about separating participant payments from staff labor costs.
relations.summary: Participant compensation should be distinguished from labor costs for field staff providing installation and operational support as job duties.

relations.reason: This one-sided diagnostic observation has no design-generalization counterpart.
relations.summary: The user tends to count session time while omitting advance setup and follow-up reporting effort.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame bases compensation on actual and ancillary burden, addresses modality, withdrawal, longitudinal reporting and payment methods, distinguishes staff labor, and identifies commonly omitted participant effort.
reports.reference_only: The reference emphasizes explicit exclusions, transfer conditions, analytic generalization, and the risk of extending findings from accessible samples too broadly.
